login.accessKey: The public half of an access key, starting with access_. Create keys under Administer, Credentials.
login.secretKey: The private half of the access key. It was shown once when the key was created or rotated.
login.submit: Check the credentials with the server and open the console for your tenant.
login.tenantSelect: Your email belongs to more than one tenant. Pick the one to sign in to.
login.useDefaults: Fill in the seeded local administrator account. Only shown when the server is on this machine.

table.selectAll: Select or clear every row on this page, for example to delete them together.
table.selectRow: Select this row for a bulk action such as delete.
table.sortServer: {{tip}} Click to sort the whole list by this column; click again to reverse the order.
table.sortPageOnly: {{tip}} Click to sort the rows on this page only; the server cannot sort by this column.
table.clearSelection: Unselect every selected row without changing anything.
table.pageSize: How many rows to load per page. Larger pages take longer to load. The choice is remembered per table.
table.first: Go to the first page of results.
table.prev: Go back one page of results.
table.jump: Type a page number between 1 and {{total}} and press Enter to jump straight to it.
table.next: Go forward one page of results.
table.last: Go to the last page of results.
table.refresh: Reload this list from the server now, keeping your page, filters, and sort.
table.autoRefresh: Reload this data automatically on a timer. Off keeps it still while you read.
table.selectColumns: Choose which columns the table shows. Your choice is remembered per table in this browser.
table.columnPinned: {{column}} is always shown because rows cannot be identified without it.
table.actionsFor: Open the actions for {{name}}: view, edit, duplicate, view JSON, delete, and record-specific actions.
table.actionsMenu: Open the actions available for this row.
table.actionsColumn: Per-row actions. Click the three dots to view, edit, duplicate, inspect the JSON, or delete.
table.search: Type part of a name to narrow the list. The search runs on the server after you stop typing.
table.clearFilters: Remove the search text and every filter and show the full list again.
table.bulkDelete: Delete every selected row. You will be asked to confirm first.

filters.status: Show only records in this state. Choose All to remove the filter.
filters.kind: Show only records of one kind. Choose All to remove the filter.
filters.eventType: Show only audit events of one type, such as failed sign-ins or secret changes.
filters.fromUtc: Show only records created at or after this time (your local time zone).
filters.toUtc: Show only records created before this time (your local time zone).
filters.method: Show only requests that used this HTTP method.
filters.statusCode: Show only requests that returned this HTTP status code, for example 404 or 500.
filters.pathContains: Show only requests whose path contains this text, for example /agents.
filters.tenantId: Show only requests made in this tenant. Leave empty for every tenant.
filters.apply: Run the search with the filter values above.
filters.clear: Reset every filter above to empty and search again.
filters.effect: Show only calls with this effect: Read, Write, or Destructive.
filters.agentProfileId: Show only records that belong to one agent profile. Choose All to remove the filter.
filters.source: Show only conversations that started on one surface.
filters.userId: Show only records of one user. Paste a user ID; the list updates when you stop typing.
filters.connectorType: Show only resources of one connector type, such as SSH or PostgreSQL.
filters.environment: Show only resources tagged with this environment, for example prod.
filters.health: Show only resources in this health state.
filters.healthStatus: Show only model endpoints in this health state.
filters.provider: Show only model endpoints of one provider.
filters.surface: Show only calls made from one surface: chat, MCP, A2A, OpenAI-compatible, or REST.
filters.decision: Show only calls with this safety decision, such as denied or approval required.
filters.resourceId: Show only calls against one resource.
filters.toolName: Show only calls to this tool, for example sql_query. The list updates when you stop typing.
filters.principalId: Show only records of one principal. Paste an ID; the list updates when you stop typing.
filters.principalType: Show only sessions of administrators, users, or credentials.
filters.visibility: Show only private or tenant-wide records.
filters.activeLayer: Show only templates whose text comes from this layer.
filters.customized: Show templates by which layer was customized, or whose default changed since.

form.option: Include {{option}} in {{field}}. Checked options are saved; unchecked ones are left out.
form.reveal: Show the typed value in plain text so you can check it before saving.
form.hide: Mask the value again so people looking at your screen cannot read it.
form.key: Key for this entry of {{field}}. Keys must be unique within the list.
form.value: Value for this entry of {{field}}. Templates and secret references are allowed where noted.
form.removeRow: Remove this entry from the list. Nothing is saved until you click Save.
form.addRow: Add an empty key and value entry to {{field}}.
form.moveUp: Move this item one place earlier. Order matters here, for example for argument lists.
form.moveDown: Move this item one place later. Order matters here, for example for argument lists.
form.removeItem: Remove this item from the list. Nothing is saved until you click Save.
form.addItem: Add a new, empty item to {{field}} and fill in its fields.

actions.openDetail: Open the full detail page for this record.
actions.view: Open this record read-only to see every field without risk of changing it.
actions.edit: Open this record in a form to change it. Changes apply when you click Save.
actions.duplicate: Start a new record prefilled with this one's values and a -copy name. Nothing is created until you save.
actions.viewJson: Show the raw JSON exactly as the API returns it, for debugging or copying into scripts.
actions.delete: Permanently delete this record. You will be asked to confirm, and it cannot be undone.
actions.add: Create a new record of this type in a form.
actions.switchToEdit: Switch this read-only view to an editable form.
actions.retryLoad: Try loading this data from the server again.
actions.dismiss: Hide this message. It comes back if the problem happens again.

modal.close: Close this window. Nothing on the server changes.
modal.dismiss: Close this window without saving. You can also press Escape.
modal.cancelForm: Close the form and discard unsaved changes.
modal.back: Go to the previous step of the form. Values you entered are kept.
modal.next: Go to the next step of the form. Nothing is saved until you click Save.
modal.saveEdit: Save your changes to this record. The server validates them and reports any field that needs attention.
modal.saveCreate: Create the record with these values. The server validates them and reports any field that needs attention.
modal.saveValue: Send the value to the server. It is encrypted on arrival and never shown again.

confirm.bulkDelete: Yes, permanently delete every selected record.
confirm.danger: Carry out this destructive action. It cannot be undone.
confirm.confirm: Carry out the action described above.

copy.id: Copy the record ID to the clipboard, for use with the REST API, SDKs, or filters.
copy.value: Copy this value to the clipboard.
copy.block: Copy the whole block to the clipboard, ready to paste into a terminal or file.

ranges.hour: Show the last 60 minutes, in one-minute buckets.
ranges.day: Show the last 24 hours. Buckets are sized so the chart stays readable.
ranges.week: Show the last 7 days. Buckets are sized so the chart stays readable.
ranges.month: Show the last 30 days. Buckets are sized so the chart stays readable.
ranges.custom: Pick your own start and end time. Very long ranges are rejected by the server.

chart.refresh: Reload the chart data from the server now.
chart.tenant: Show request activity for one tenant or for every tenant on the server.

badges.active: Active: this record is in use.
badges.inactive: Inactive: this record is kept but ignored until it is turned back on.
badges.builtIn: Built-in: shipped with Hugo and read-only. Clone it to make a version you can edit.
badges.custom: Custom: created in this tenant, so it can be edited and deleted.
badges.systemAdmin: System administrator: can manage every tenant and bypasses authorization checks.
badges.tenantAdmin: Tenant administrator: can manage everything inside this tenant.
badges.user: Regular user: access comes only from role assignments.
badges.role: This assignment grants the {{role}} role and every permission in it.
badges.defaultProfile: The tenant default profile: callers that name no profile get this one.
badges.expiringSoon: This secret expires within 14 days. Replace its values or extend the expiry before resources stop working.
badges.lockdown: This tenant is locked down: only read calls are allowed until a tenant administrator lifts it.
badges.locked: Locked to its profile: the credential can only act as the bound profile, whatever the caller asks for.

permissions.source: The role this grant comes from. Fix access by changing that role or the assignment that grants it.
permissions.type: Permit grants the operations; Deny blocks them even when another role permits them.
permissions.resources: The kinds of records this grant covers, such as Resource, Secret, or Agent profile.
permissions.operations: What may be done to those records, such as Read, Create, or Execute.
permissions.scope: Tenant scope covers every record of the type; Resource scope covers one specific record.

secretOnce.accessKey: The public access key. It identifies the credential and is safe to store in configuration.
secretOnce.secretKey: The secret key. This is the only time it is shown; copy it into your password manager or secret store now.
secretOnce.done: Close this window. The secret key cannot be retrieved later, only rotated.
secretOnce.snippet: Ready-to-paste MCP client configuration that uses this access key. The secret key is read from an environment variable.

promptTemplateKind.System: A system prompt: the standing instructions that set up the agent.
promptTemplateKind.Task: A task prompt: wraps the caller's message into what the agent receives.
promptTemplateKind.Fragment: A reusable piece included by other templates with {{> name}}.
promptTemplateKind.ToolDescription: Text that describes an agent as an MCP tool or A2A skill.
promptTemplateKind.ConfigFile: The content of a generated configuration file, such as an MCP config.
promptTemplateKind.Other: Any other text Hugo renders into instructions.

permissionType.Deny: Deny: blocks the listed operations, even when another permission allows them.

effect.Read: Read: looks at data without changing anything, such as a SELECT or listing files.
effect.Write: Write: changes something that can be changed back, such as an INSERT or uploading a file.
effect.Destructive: Destructive: deletes, drops, restarts, or otherwise cannot be undone. Waits for approval by default.

accessMode.ReadOnly: Read only: the agent can look but write and destructive tools are not even listed.
accessMode.ReadWriteWithApproval: Read and write with approval: every write or destructive call waits for a person.
accessMode.ReadWrite: Read and write: writes run directly; destructive calls still wait unless the binding opts out.

approvalStatus.Pending: Pending: waiting for a person to approve or reject it.
approvalStatus.Approved: Approved: a person allowed the call and it ran.
approvalStatus.Rejected: Rejected: a person refused the call; the agent was told.
approvalStatus.Expired: Expired: nobody decided in time, so the call was refused.
approvalStatus.Cancelled: Cancelled: the turn ended or the tenant was locked down before a decision.

toolDecision.Allowed: Allowed: the access mode let the call run without asking.
toolDecision.Denied: Denied: the access mode, a tool rule, or lockdown refused the call.
toolDecision.ApprovalRequired: Approval required: the call waited for a person.
toolDecision.Approved: Approved: a person allowed the call.
toolDecision.Rejected: Rejected: a person refused the call.
toolDecision.Cancelled: Cancelled: the pending approval was withdrawn or cancelled by lockdown.

toolStatus.Succeeded: Succeeded: the tool ran and returned a result.
toolStatus.Failed: Failed: the tool or the target system returned an error.
toolStatus.TimedOut: Timed out: the tool did not finish within its timeout.
toolStatus.Cancelled: Cancelled: the turn was stopped while the tool was running.
toolStatus.Pending: Pending: waiting for an approval before it can run.
toolStatus.Running: Running: the tool is executing now.
toolStatus.NotExecuted: Not executed: the call was denied, rejected, or only classified (dry run).

healthStatus.Healthy: Healthy: the last check reached the system and it answered normally.
healthStatus.Degraded: Degraded: the system answered, but slowly or with warnings.
healthStatus.Unhealthy: Unhealthy: the last check could not reach the system or it answered with an error.
healthStatus.Unknown: Not checked yet: no connection test or health check has run.

secretKind.Password: A password, optionally with its username.
secretKind.PrivateKey: An SSH or TLS private key, optionally with its passphrase.
secretKind.ApiToken: An API or bearer token issued by a service.
secretKind.AccessKeyPair: An access key ID and secret access key, such as AWS keys.
secretKind.ServiceAccountJson: A cloud service account key file in JSON, such as Google Cloud.
secretKind.Kubeconfig: A Kubernetes kubeconfig file with cluster and user credentials.
secretKind.ConnectionString: A full connection string that includes credentials.
secretKind.Certificate: A certificate with its private key, for mutual TLS.

connectorCategory.Compute: Hosts and machines reached over SSH or similar.
connectorCategory.Storage: Object storage such as S3, Azure Blob, and Google Cloud Storage.
connectorCategory.Logging: Log services such as Papertrail and Loki.
connectorCategory.Cloud: Cloud control planes such as AWS.
connectorCategory.Orchestration: Container orchestration such as Kubernetes and Docker.
connectorCategory.Observability: Metrics and monitoring such as Prometheus and SolarWinds.
connectorCategory.Agent: Other agents reached over MCP or A2A.
connectorCategory.Other: Connectors that fit no other category.

surface.Chat: Dashboard chat with Hugo's own agent loop.
surface.Mcp: An MCP client such as Claude Code drove the call.
surface.A2A: Another agent called this profile over A2A.
surface.OpenAI: An OpenAI-compatible client talked to the profile.
surface.Rest: A direct REST or SDK tool invocation.

modelKind.Embedding: Turns text into vectors for retrieval.

visibility.Private: Only the owner can use it.
visibility.Tenant: Everyone with access in the tenant can use it.

auditEventType.AuthorizationDenied: A principal tried something its permissions do not allow.
auditEventType.SecretRevealed: Someone revealed a secret's plaintext, with a reason.
auditEventType.LockdownChanged: A tenant administrator turned lockdown on or off.
auditEventType.HostKeyMismatch: An SSH host presented a different key than the pinned one; the connection was refused.
auditEventType.SessionReauthenticated: A user re-entered their password on a session (needed before revealing secrets).
auditEventType.PermissionChanged: A permission was created, changed, or deleted.
auditEventType.ConfigurationChanged: A configuration record changed (for example a prompt template or profile setting).
auditEventType.PasswordChanged: A user changed their password, or an administrator reset it.
auditEventType.RestartRequested: Someone asked the server to restart.
auditEventType.KnowledgeChanged: Resource knowledge was written or deleted by an operator, agent, or model.
auditEventType.ModelEndpointChanged: A model endpoint was created, changed, or deleted.
auditEventType.SettingLearned: A connector recorded a setting on first use, for example an SSH host key.

knowledgeSource.Operator: Written or edited by a person in the dashboard or API.
knowledgeSource.Generated: Drafted by a model with sql_generate_context. Review before relying on it.
knowledgeSource.Agent: Recorded by an agent during its work (sql_update_context). Unverified.
knowledgeSource.Derived: Computed by Hugo from the crawl, not written by a person or model.

tenants.add: Create a new tenant: an isolated space with its own users, resources, secrets, and profiles.
tenants.name: Display name of the tenant. People pick the tenant by its ID when they sign in.
tenants.description: Who or what this tenant is for, for example a team or customer.
tenants.active: Inactive tenants cannot sign in or call tools. Their data is kept.
tenants.region: Optional region label for this tenant, for your own bookkeeping.
tenants.lockdown: A locked-down tenant denies every call that is not a read.

users.add: Create a person who signs in with email and password. Give them access with a role assignment afterwards.
users.email: The address the person signs in with. Unique within the tenant.
users.name: First and last name, shown in audit records and lists.
users.role: Administrator level of the account. Ordinary users get access through role assignments.
users.password: Sign-in password. When editing, leave it empty to keep the current password.
users.firstName: Given name, shown in lists and audit records.
users.lastName: Family name, shown in lists and audit records.
users.isTenantAdmin: Tenant administrators can manage everything inside this tenant, including users and secrets.
users.isAdmin: System administrators manage every tenant and bypass authorization. Grant sparingly.
users.active: Inactive users cannot sign in, and their access keys stop working.

actions.permissions: Show every permission this user ends up with after combining all roles and assignments.
actions.resetPassword: Set a temporary password; the user must change it at next sign-in.
actions.assignRole: Open Assignments filtered to this user to grant a role.

users.mustChangePassword: The user must choose a new password at their next sign-in.

credentials.add: Create an access key for a script, SDK, or service. The secret is shown once after saving.
credentials.name: What this key is for, for example claude-code-laptop. Helps you find it before rotating or deleting.
credentials.accessKey: The public half of the key, sent with every request. Safe to store in configuration.
credentials.secretKeyLast4: The last four characters of the secret, so you can match a key without seeing it.
credentials.userId: The user who owns this key. A key can never do more than its owner.
credentials.lastUsedUtc: When the key last authenticated a request. Old dates point to unused keys you can delete.
credentials.authMode: How the key may authenticate: sent directly, signed per request, exchanged for a session, or any of these (Hybrid).
credentials.expiresUtc: After this time the key stops working. Leave empty for a key that does not expire.
credentials.active: Inactive keys are rejected but kept, so you can turn them back on.

actions.rotate: Replace the secret with a new one. The old secret stops working immediately; the new one is shown once.
actions.permissions: Show every permission this key ends up with after combining its owner, roles, and assignments.
actions.scopes: Open the credential scope assignments filtered to this credential.

credentials.agentProfileId: The profile this credential acts as by default. Harnesses should use a bound credential.
credentials.lockToProfile: When on, the credential can only act as its bound profile, whatever the caller requests.

roles.add: Create a custom role, then add permissions to it and assign it to users or keys.
roles.name: Name people see when assigning the role, for example Release Operator.
roles.description: What the role is for and who should get it.
roles.active: Inactive roles grant nothing, even where they are assigned.

actions.clone: Make an editable copy of this built-in role that you can adjust.

permissions.add: Create a rule that permits or denies operations on resource types.
permissions.name: Short name for the rule, shown when you build roles.
permissions.permissionType: Permit allows the operations below. Deny blocks them and always wins over a permit.
permissions.resourceTypes: Which kinds of records the rule covers. All covers every type.
permissions.operationTypes: Which operations the rule covers, such as Read, Create, or Execute (invoke).

userAssignments.add: Give a user a role, for the whole tenant or for one specific record.
userAssignments.userId: The person who receives the role.
userAssignments.roleName: The role granted. The person gets every permission in it.
userAssignments.roleId: The role to grant. The person gets every permission in it.
userAssignments.resourceScope: Tenant applies the role to every record. Resource limits it to the one record named below.
userAssignments.resourceId: Identifier of the single record the role applies to, for example an agent ID.
userAssignments.inheritsToChildren: Apply the role to every record in the tenant, including ones created later.
userAssignments.active: Inactive assignments grant nothing but are kept.

credentialAssignments.add: Give an access key a role, for the whole tenant or for one specific record.
credentialAssignments.credentialId: The access key that receives the role. It still cannot exceed its owner.
credentialAssignments.roleName: The role granted to the key.
credentialAssignments.roleId: The role to grant. Pick the narrowest role that lets the automation do its job.
credentialAssignments.resourceScope: Tenant applies the role to every record. Resource limits it to the one record named below.
credentialAssignments.resourceId: Identifier of the single record the role applies to, for example the one agent a CI job may invoke.
credentialAssignments.inheritsToChildren: Apply the role to every record in the tenant, including ones created later.
credentialAssignments.active: Inactive assignments grant nothing but are kept.

actions.clone: Copy this template under a new name you choose, then open the copy in the editor.

promptTemplates.add: Write a new prompt template in the editor with live preview. Each save becomes a version.
promptTemplates.name: Template name, unique in the tenant. Includes refer to templates by name.
promptTemplates.kind: What the template is used for: system prompt, task wrapper, fragment, tool description, or config file.
promptTemplates.currentVersion: The newest saved version. Every save keeps the previous text as a version you can restore.
promptTemplates.description: What the template does and where it is used.
promptTemplates.key: The template key. Connectors use connector.<type>.instructions; personas use persona.<name>.
promptTemplates.source: Where the Built-in comes from: hugo for core templates, or the connector type.
promptTemplates.activeLayer: The layer whose text is used now: Tenant, then Global, then Built-in.
promptTemplates.tenantLayer: This tenant's override, with its version.
promptTemplates.globalLayer: The Global default for every tenant, with its version.
promptTemplates.lastUpdateUtc: When the Tenant or Global layer was last saved.
promptTemplates.defaultUpdated: The default below this layer changed after it was customized. Open the template to compare and adopt.

audit.createdUtc: When the event happened, in your local time zone.
audit.eventType: What kind of security or configuration event this was.
audit.principalName: Who did it: an administrator, a user, or an access key.
audit.resource: The kind of record and the operation involved, for example Agent / Read.
audit.reason: Why the event happened or why access was denied.
audit.sourceIp: Network address the request came from.
audit.principalType: Whether the actor was an administrator, a user, or an access key.
audit.principalId: Identifier of the administrator, user, or access key that acted.
audit.resourceType: Kind of record involved, such as Agent or Secret.
audit.operation: Operation that was attempted, such as Read or Execute.
audit.path: Path of the request that caused the event.
audit.authResult: Outcome of checking who the caller is.
audit.authorizationResult: Outcome of checking what the caller may do.
audit.bypassReason: Why authorization was skipped, for example a system administrator.
audit.statusCode: HTTP status returned to the caller.
audit.requestId: Request identifier. Search Request History or the server logs with it.

approvals.bulkReject: Reject every selected approval at once. Each caller is told its action was refused.
approvals.summary: The exact action waiting for approval, for example running a command on a host.
approvals.effect: How the call was classified: Write changes something, Destructive deletes or restarts.
approvals.status: Pending waits for a person; the other states are final.
approvals.agentProfileId: The profile whose binding required the approval.
approvals.requestedBy: The principal (user, credential, or agent run) that made the call.
approvals.createdUtc: When the agent proposed the call.
approvals.expiresUtc: When the request expires if nobody decides. Expired calls are refused.
approvals.decidedBy: Who approved or rejected the call.
approvals.decisionNote: The note the approver left with the decision.
approvals.fromUtc: Show approvals requested at or after this time.

actions.decide: Open the approval card to approve or reject this call with a note.
actions.invocation: Open the tool invocation record behind this approval.
actions.cancel: Withdraw this pending call so it never runs. The requester or an approver can cancel.

bindings.resourceId: The resource this binding attaches. One resource can be bound to many profiles.
bindings.alias: The name the agent uses for this resource in tool calls and instructions, for example prod-db.
bindings.accessMode: Read only, read and write with approval for risky calls, or read and write. Decides what the agent may do.
bindings.requireApprovalForDestructive: Even in read and write mode, destructive calls (deletes, restarts, drops) wait for a person. On by default.
bindings.instructionMode: Inherit uses the connector's and resource's instructions; Append adds your text; Replace uses only your text.
bindings.instructionText: Extra or replacement instructions for this resource in this profile, for example which schemas matter.
bindings.maxOutputBytes: Cap on tool output from this resource, tighter than the connector default. Leave empty for the default.
bindings.maxRows: Cap on rows returned by queries on this resource. Leave empty for the connector default.
bindings.enabled: Disabled bindings are kept but hidden from the agent, as if the resource were not bound.
bindings.denyPatterns: Regular expressions matched against the command or statement of per-call classified tools. A match denies the call.
bindings.allowKnowledgeUpdates: When off, tools that save knowledge about this resource (such as table context) return drafts instead of saving.

models.apiKeySecretId: The secret holding this provider's API key or credentials. Stored encrypted; never shown to the model.
models.add: Add an inference or embedding model endpoint for Hugo's own agent loop.
models.kind: Inference models answer chat turns; embedding models turn text into vectors for retrieval.
models.provider: Which API the endpoint speaks. OpenAI-compatible covers vLLM, LM Studio, and similar servers.
models.baseUrl: Where the provider API listens, for example http://127.0.0.1:11434 for a local Ollama.
models.model: The provider's model name, for example llama3.1, gpt-4o, or claude-sonnet.
models.apiKey: The provider API key. Stored as an encrypted secret and referenced by the endpoint.
models.region: Cloud region for providers that need one, such as Bedrock or Vertex.
models.deploymentName: The Azure OpenAI deployment that serves the model.
models.apiVersion: The Azure OpenAI API version to call.
models.contextWindowTokens: How many tokens the model accepts. Hugo compacts history before reaching it.
models.maxOutputTokens: Upper bound on tokens the model may produce in one answer.
models.embeddingDimensions: Vector size the embedding model produces. Filled in by Validate when left empty.
models.supportsTools: Whether the model can call tools. Chat needs this for anything beyond plain answers.
models.supportsStreaming: Whether answers can stream token by token.
models.maxConcurrency: How many requests Hugo sends to this endpoint at once.
models.timeoutSeconds: How long one model request may take before it fails.
models.maxRetries: How many times a failed request is retried before giving up.
models.healthStatus: Result of the last validation or background health check.
models.lastHealthUtc: When the endpoint was last checked.

sections.endpoint: Which provider and model this is, and how to reach it.
sections.capabilities: What the model can do and how much text it handles.
sections.limits: Concurrency, timeouts, and retries for calls to this endpoint.

actions.validate: Send a tiny prompt (or embed a short text) and record the latency and result.
actions.listModels: Ask the provider which models it offers, where the provider supports listing.

resources.name: Unique name for this resource in the tenant. Bindings use it as the default alias the agent sees.
resources.connectorType: Which kind of system this is (SSH, PostgreSQL, S3, and so on). It decides the settings, secrets, and tools.
resources.environment: Free tag such as prod or staging. The agent sees it, which helps it treat production carefully.
resources.add: Add a connection to a system: pick a connector, fill in its settings, choose its secrets, and test it.
resources.displayName: Optional friendly name for people. The agent uses the name or the binding alias.
resources.visibility: Private resources are usable by their owner; tenant resources by every profile in the tenant.
resources.defaultAccessModeCeiling: The most a binding may grant on this resource. Leave empty to allow any access mode.
resources.endpoint: Short summary of where the resource lives. Searchable, and shown to the agent.
resources.description: What this resource is, for people reading the list.
resources.notes: Operator notes the agent receives in its instructions, such as which tables matter or what never to touch.
resources.health: Result of the last connection test or health sweep.
resources.lastTestUtc: When the connection was last tested.

sections.general: Name, environment, and notes the agent reads.
sections.connector: The connector, its settings, and its secrets.

actions.test: Test the saved settings and secrets against the real system now.
actions.tryTool: Dry run and then execute one of this resource's tools as a chosen profile.
actions.referrers: List the profiles and bindings that use this resource.

secrets.name: Unique name for this secret in the tenant. Resources and model endpoints pick it by name.
secrets.kind: What the secret holds. The kind decides which fields it has and which connector slots accept it.
secrets.saveValue: Encrypt and store the new values. Fields left empty keep their stored values.
secrets.add: Store a new secret: choose its kind and fill in the values, or import them from a file.
secrets.description: What the secret is for and who owns it. Never put secret values here.
secrets.expiresUtc: When the credential stops working, so Hugo can warn before it expires.
secrets.fingerprint: A non-reversible hint, such as the last characters or an SSH key fingerprint, to tell secrets apart.
secrets.referrerCount: How many resources and model endpoints use this secret.
secrets.lastRotatedUtc: When the values were last replaced.
secrets.lastRevealedUtc: When someone last revealed the plaintext through the audited reveal.

sections.values: The secret values for this kind. They are encrypted before they are stored.

actions.replaceValues: Replace some or all of the values; fields you leave empty keep their stored values.
actions.reveal: Show the plaintext values after stating a reason and re-entering your password. Audited.
actions.referrers: List the resources and model endpoints that use this secret.

profiles.add: Create an agent profile: a persona, models, limits, and the surfaces that expose it.
profiles.name: URL-safe name, unique in the tenant. MCP clients reach the profile at /mcp/{name} and A2A at .../{name}.
profiles.displayName: Friendly name shown in the dashboard and in the A2A agent card.
profiles.description: What this profile is for. Shown to people and in the A2A card summary.
profiles.personaName: What the agent calls itself in conversation. The default profile uses Agent Smith.
profiles.userAddress: How the agent addresses the caller. The default profile says Mr. Anderson.
profiles.visibility: Private profiles are visible to their owner; tenant profiles to everyone with access in the tenant.

profiles.fallbackInferenceEndpointId: Used when the primary model fails or is unavailable.

profiles.maxToolCallsPerTurn: Upper bound on tool calls in one turn, across every round.
profiles.toolTimeoutSeconds: How long one tool call may run before it is cancelled.
profiles.temperature: Sampling temperature for the model. Lower values make answers more deterministic.
profiles.exposeMcp: List this profile's tools and instructions to MCP clients such as Claude Code.
profiles.exposeA2a: Publish an A2A agent card and accept A2A messages for this profile.
profiles.exposeOpenai: Let OpenAI-compatible clients use this profile as a model name.

profiles.instructionsAppend: Free text appended to the compiled instructions, after every resource section.
profiles.bindingCount: How many resources are bound to this profile.
profiles.exposure: Which protocol surfaces can reach this profile.

sections.models: Which models answer for this profile in Hugo's own loop.
sections.limits: Bounds on each turn, so a runaway loop stops.
sections.exposure: Which protocol surfaces can reach this profile.

actions.chat: Open Chat to talk to this profile.
actions.duplicate: Copy this profile and its bindings under a new name, then open the copy.

conversations.agentProfileId: The profile the conversation talks to.

knowledge.add: Write context for a table or another scope that has none yet.
knowledge.select: Open this entry in the editor.
knowledge.scope: The kind of note: database, table, or a connector-specific scope such as notes.
knowledge.key: For table context, the schema-qualified table, for example main.orders. Leave empty for a scope's root entry.

knowledge.content: Concise Markdown agents read: what the data means, business definitions, caveats, and confirmed join paths.

promptTemplates.title: Prompt templates and their layers
promptTemplates.p1: Every instruction Hugo gives an agent is a template: the Agent Smith persona, the safety rules, and each connector's instructions. Templates use variables such as profile.personaName and this.alias in double braces, and each save creates a new version.
promptTemplates.p2: Templates are layered: the built-in text ships with Hugo, a global default can override it for every tenant, and a tenant can override that. Reset to Default removes an override and falls back one layer.

tenants.title: Tenants
tenants.p1: A tenant is an isolated organization on this server. Users, access keys, resources, secrets, profiles, and conversations all belong to one tenant, and nothing is visible across tenants.

users.title: Users and credentials
users.p1: A user is a person who signs in with an email and password. A credential (access key) is how automation signs in. Every access key belongs to a user and can never do more than that user can.
users.p2: Neither gets access just by existing. Access comes from the administrator flags on the user and from role assignments.

credentials.title: Credentials and users
credentials.p1: A credential is an access key and secret key pair for scripts, SDKs, and services. It belongs to a user. Its effective permissions are the overlap of what its own role assignments grant and what its owner may do.
credentials.p2: The secret key is shown once, when the key is created or rotated. Rotate keys regularly and delete ones that have not been used in a long time.

roles.title: Roles, permissions, and assignments
roles.p1: A permission is a single rule: permit or deny certain operations (such as Read, Execute, or Reveal) on certain resource types (such as Resource, Secret, or Agent profile). A role is a named bundle of permissions. Deny always wins over permit.
roles.p2: Nothing changes for anyone until a role is assigned. Assignments, on the next tab, connect a role to a user or an access key, for the whole tenant or for one record.

assignments.title: Assignments
assignments.p1: An assignment grants one role to one user or access key. Tenant scope applies the role to every record of the covered types; resource scope applies it to a single record, such as one agent profile a harness may use.
assignments.p2: Use Effective permissions on a user or credential to see the combined result of all their assignments.

audit.title: Audit and request history
audit.p1: Audit records are security and configuration events: sign-ins, denied requests, secret reveals and changes, role and binding changes, lockdowns, and restarts. They are kept for the retention period in settings.
audit.p2: Request History, on the previous tab, is the raw HTTP traffic. Use audit to answer who changed what, and request history to debug what a client actually sent.

requests.title: Request history
requests.p1: Every API request this server captured, with method, path, status, timing, headers, and bodies (truncated to the configured size). Use it to debug integrations and SDK calls. Click a bar in the chart to narrow the table to that time.

diagram.label: How secrets, resources, bindings, profiles, and surfaces relate

secret.title: Secrets
secret.tip: Passwords, keys, and tokens, encrypted in Hugo. Resources use them by slot; agents never see them.

resource.title: Resources
resource.tip: One configured system each: an SSH host, a bucket, a database, a log service, with its settings.

binding.title: Bindings
binding.tip: Attach a resource to a profile under an alias, with read only, approval, or read and write access.

profile.title: Agent profile
profile.tip: The agent: Agent Smith by default, with its models and limits. Every surface talks to a profile.

surfaces.title: Surfaces
surfaces.tip: Claude Code over MCP, other agents over A2A, scripts over REST and the SDKs, and you in chat.

profiles.title: How profiles, resources, and surfaces relate
profiles.p1: A profile is an agent: a persona (Agent Smith by default), the models it thinks with, and a set of bindings. Each binding attaches one resource under an alias with an access mode.
profiles.p2: Every surface is a client of the same profile. MCP clients get the profile's tools and instructions; chat, A2A, and OpenAI-compatible clients run Hugo's own loop with the profile's model.

approvals.title: When a call waits for a person
approvals.p1: Every tool call is classified as Read, Write, or Destructive. Destructive calls wait for approval by default, and on bindings in read and write with approval mode every write waits too.
approvals.p2: Approve to let the call run, or reject to refuse it. The agent is told either way, and the decision is recorded with your note.

conversations.title: Conversations from every surface
conversations.p1: Dashboard chat, A2A contexts, MCP delegation, and OpenAI-compatible sessions all become conversations here, so every surface's history is in one place.

resources.title: Resources, secrets, and bindings
resources.p1: A resource is one configured system: its connector, settings, and the secrets it uses. The secrets stay encrypted in Hugo; agents never see them.
resources.p2: A resource does nothing until a profile binds it. The binding decides the alias the agent sees and what it may do.

secrets.title: How secrets are protected
secrets.p1: Values are encrypted with AES-256-GCM under the master key and bound to their tenant. Resources and model endpoints reference secrets by slot.
secrets.p2: Nobody sees a value again except through Reveal, which needs the Reveal permission, a reason, and a fresh password check, and is always audited.

models.title: When Hugo needs a model
models.p1: MCP clients such as Claude Code bring their own model; Hugo only supplies tools and instructions. Chat, A2A, and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint run Hugo's own loop and need an inference model on the profile.

knowledge.title: What knowledge notes are for
knowledge.p1: Notes are facts an operator would tell a teammate. Hugo embeds them and retrieves the relevant ones into context for each turn.

toolInvocations.title: One record per tool call
toolInvocations.p1: Every tool call from every surface goes through the same pipeline: classification, the binding's access mode, approval if needed, the connector, and the secret scrubber. Each one is recorded here.

connectors.title: Connectors and resources
connectors.p1: A connector is code that knows how to talk to one family of systems. A resource is one configured instance of a connector, with its own settings and secrets.

analytics.title: Where these numbers come from
analytics.p1: Analytics aggregates tool invocations, chat turns, and model calls on the server, bucketed by time and scoped to this tenant.

sessions.title: Sessions and tokens
sessions.p1: Signing in or exchanging an access key issues a session token. Revoking a session ends it at once, wherever it is being used.

plugins.title: Connector plugins
plugins.p1: Plugins add connector types from the plugins directory without rebuilding Hugo. They load only when Connectors.EnablePlugins is on.
